translation: But by name, [this] is drawn out from the Vātula tantra, like ghee [skimmed] up to its measure.
And just as honey [is drawn] from a flower, this auspicious [work] is the essence drawn from the essence.
The beginning of this scripture is only to show the epitome of the mantras — [text corrupt in the middle].
The supreme seed named 'sā', which abides in all beings.

sanskrit: sthānāntareṣu pravibhajyamāno varṇatvamāgacchati yaḥ sa śabdaḥ || iti ||
translation: That [sound] which, being distributed among the different [articulatory] places, comes to be a phoneme — that is śabda.
And that, because it is being guarded, abides in all beings.

sanskrit: cāsmābhirmṛgendra vṛttidīpikāyām | iti || tata eva cāvadhāryaḥ | asya ca
translation: —and by us in the Mṛgendra Vṛtti-dīpikā. Thus. From that very [source] it is to be ascertained. And of this—

sanskrit: taṃ viditvā mahāsena deśikaḥ pāśahā bhavet | iti ||
translation: Having known that, O Mahāsena, the teacher would become a destroyer of the bonds.
Beings that have gone within the water — they ... (text corrupt).

sanskrit: na prakāśaḥ prakāśena sa hi pratyavamarśinī || iti ||
translation: Light is not [made manifest] by [another] light, for it is possessed of reflexive awareness.
He should perform the rite as he wishes.
The extraction of the denotative mantra is indeed just the concise [form] of that whose utterance is the gross word.

sanskrit: akṣarāntaritaṃ kṛtvā sa ṣaḍaṅgaḥ śivo bhavet ||
translation: Having made it interspersed with syllables, that [mantra] becomes six-limbed Śiva.
That seed called 'ahaṅkāra' is said in the Sāmāna-tantra to end in -s and to be all-pervading — thus.
The unutterable, the undoubted, is prescribed for liberation — thus [the section] beginning with Sakala-Niṣkala.
The fourteenth chapter (the division).

sanskrit: etanme brūhi sadbhāvaṃ kāruṇyāt tu maheśvara || 1 ||
translation: Tell me this true nature, O Maheśvara, out of compassion.
[text corrupt] ... standing athwart ... — but he is everywhere.
Having known [it], one would not be released if the dissolution of this [body?] should occur.

sanskrit: vetyevamimāṃ vyāptiṃ sa yāpī tu na saṃśayaḥ || 4 ||
translation: Thus this pervasion ... but there is no doubt.
Having known the all-pervading god, one is released; here there is no doubt.
